findings.title: No baseline training code or convergence logs; 4.4x/1.7x speedup not reproducible from repo
findings.quote: converging 4.4x faster than consistency models and 1.7x faster than rectified flow models
findings.claim: The repo trains and evaluates only Consistency-FM: `run_lib.py:95-99` (and `run_lib_pytorch.py:99-103`) raise NotImplementedError for any SDE other than 'consistencyfm', and `configs/` contains only consistencyfm configs; training loops log training/eval loss and sample grids but never FID-vs-iteration curves for any method.
findings.concern: The headline training-efficiency claims (abstract, Fig. 1 bubble plot, Fig. 4 convergence curves) compare Consistency-FM's convergence against Consistency-Model and Rectified-Flow convergence curves that cannot be produced from this repository, so the central efficiency result is not reproducible here.
findings.resolution: Provide the baseline training scripts/configs (or the logged FID-vs-step curves) used to derive the 4.4x and 1.7x convergence factors under matched compute.
findings.reason: Quote confirmed at paper_text.txt (matches abstract/intro wording verbatim); run_lib.py:95/99 and run_lib_pytorch.py:99/103 raise NotImplementedError exactly as cited, and configs/ contains only configs/consistencyfm/* (cifar10, celeba_hq, afhq_cat) -- no consistency-model or rectified-flow configs or training paths exist in the repo.

findings.title: No AFHQ/CelebA checkpoints; reference FID stats not in repo (CIFAR stats/ckpt external)
findings.quote: For a quick start, we have provided CIFAR-10 checkpoints at [this link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1KlHPe2RYg75Zq4BKb0k1GQMWsNhrjLzb/view?usp=sharing).
findings.claim: Only CIFAR-10 checkpoints are offered (one Google-Drive link); no AFHQ-Cat or CelebA-HQ checkpoints are provided. The reference FID statistics are not in the repo either: `evaluation.py:46` loads `assets/stats/cifar10_stats.npz`, but `assets/` does not exist in the clone, and high-res FID needs self-generated clean-fid custom stats.
findings.concern: Reproducing Table 3 (AFHQ-Cat 22.5, CelebA-HQ 36.4) requires retraining 256x256 models for 250k iterations plus regenerating clean-fid stats, and even the CIFAR Table 2 numbers depend on external downloads (checkpoints + cifar10_stats.npz) whose links cannot be verified in this sandbox.
findings.resolution: Release the high-resolution checkpoints and the exact FID reference-stat files (or a fetch script), and confirm the Google-Drive links resolve.
findings.reason: Quote matches README.md:72 verbatim; evaluation.py:46 confirmed to reference 'assets/stats/cifar10_stats.npz'; a repo-wide search found no assets/ directory and no AFHQ/CelebA checkpoint link anywhere in README.md, only training commands for those datasets.

findings.title: ConsistencyFM ignores config hyperparameters; boundary is hardcoded to 1, so the two-stage curriculum never runs
findings.claim: `ConsistencyFM.__init__` accepts `consistencyfm_hyperparameters` (passed as `config.consistencyfm.to_dict()` at run_lib.py:96 and run_lib_pytorch.py:100/224) but never assigns it; instead `self.consistencyfm_hyperparameters` is unconditionally set to this hardcoded dict. `losses.py` reads only `sde.consistencyfm_hyperparameters`, so the effective values are always delta=1e-3, num_segments=2, boundary=1, alpha=1e-5. `_audit_code/check_hyperparams_ignored.py` confirms the init param is unused (`assigned_from_param=False`) and boundary is hardcoded to 1 while all three configs request boundary=0.9.
findings.concern: The documented two-stage boundary curriculum (README:47-49 runs `--config.consistencyfm.boundary 0` then `0.9`) and every config/CLI hyperparameter override are silently discarded; training always uses boundary=1, so the released code cannot execute the documented training procedure and — if the reported FID numbers relied on the boundary-0->0.9 schedule — cannot reproduce them.
findings.resolution: Assign `self.consistencyfm_hyperparameters = consistencyfm_hyperparameters` (after fixing the delta key, see config-key-delta-mismatch) and state which boundary schedule produced the reported Table 2/3 numbers.
findings.reason: Quote matches sde_lib.py:34-39 verbatim; re-ran check_hyperparams_ignored.py which confirms assigned_from_param=False, hardcoded_boundary='1', and all three configs request boundary='0.9', exactly matching the claim.

findings.title: Config key `delta_t` never matches the loss key `delta` (latent KeyError, masked by hardcoding)
findings.quote:
config.consistencyfm = consistencyfm = ml_collections.ConfigDict()
  consistencyfm.delta_t = 1e-3
  consistencyfm.num_segments = 2
  consistencyfm.boundary = 0.9
  consistencyfm.alpha = 1e-5
findings.claim: All three configs name the time-interval hyperparameter `delta_t`, but the loss reads `hyperparameter["delta"]` (losses.py:167 and 225). Because the config dict is discarded (see hardcoded-hyperparameters-ignore-config), this never surfaces; `_audit_code/check_hyperparams_ignored.py` shows config key = `delta_t` vs loss keys = ['alpha','boundary','delta','num_segments'].
findings.concern: If the primary hardcoding bug were fixed so the config dict were actually used, losses.py:167 `hyperparameter["delta"]` would raise KeyError on every run; the two defects mask each other, indicating the config->loss path was never exercised.
findings.resolution: Rename the config key `delta_t` to `delta` (or make the loss read `delta_t`) and wire the config through `ConsistencyFM.__init__`.
findings.reason: Quote matches configs/consistencyfm/cifar10_gaussian_ddpmpp.py:50-54 verbatim; grep confirms losses.py:167 and :225 read hyperparameter["delta"], and check_hyperparams_ignored.py confirms all three configs use the key delta_t, exactly as claimed.

findings.title: README CIFAR eval asks for checkpoints 34-40 the released config never produces (eval hangs)
findings.claim: `run_lib.py` saves `checkpoint_{step//snapshot_freq}.pth`; the CIFAR config sets snapshot_freq=20000 (cifar10_gaussian_ddpmpp.py:32) and the two-stage README training reaches 200001 iters, so only checkpoint_0..10 are produced. The eval command requests begin_ckpt 34 / end_ckpt 40; `run_lib.py:272` then sleeps in a `while not exists(checkpoint_34.pth)` loop forever. `_audit_code/check_ckpt_indices.py` reports max reachable index ~10-12 and an implied cadence of ~5000.
findings.concern: A user following the README literally (train from scratch, then run the eval command) hangs indefinitely; the eval indices imply snapshot_freq ~5000, inconsistent with the released 20000, so the command is only usable with the separately downloaded checkpoints whose numbering is undocumented.
findings.resolution: Align snapshot_freq (or eval begin/end_ckpt) between config and README, and state the checkpoint numbering of the provided CIFAR checkpoints.
findings.reason: Quote matches README.md:64-67 verbatim; re-ran check_ckpt_indices.py which confirms max_reachable_ckpt_index=12 (CIFAR-only would be 10, matching the claim), begin_ckpt=34 unreachable, and run_lib.py:272 contains the cited 'while not tf.io.gfile.exists(...)' wait loop.

findings.title: `(threshold, int)` builds a tuple instead of isinstance() in two loss guards
findings.claim: `(threshold, int)` is a 2-tuple (always truthy), so the guard reduces to `threshold == 0`; the intended `isinstance(threshold, int)` is written correctly elsewhere (losses.py:203-204). The same tuple mistake recurs in `masked_losses_v` at losses.py:219-220.
findings.concern: Currently harmless because boundary is hardcoded to the int 1 (see hardcoded-hyperparameters-ignore-config) so the `== 0` branch never fires; but if boundary were ever the float 0.0 the tuple form would wrongly early-return `x_at_segment_ends` / skip the velocity loss, exactly the fragility the sde_lib.py:37 comment warns about.
findings.resolution: Replace `(threshold, int)` with `isinstance(threshold, int)` at losses.py:184 and losses.py:220.
findings.reason: Quote matches losses.py:183-185 verbatim; grep confirms the correct isinstance() form at losses.py:203 and the recurrence of the tuple bug at losses.py:219-220 exactly as claimed.

findings.title: config.seed=42 declared but never applied; runs are unseeded
findings.claim: `config.seed = 42` is defined in both default configs but never consumed: a repo-wide grep finds no `torch.manual_seed` / `np.random.seed(config.seed)` / `set_seed`. The only seeding calls are bare `np.random.seed()` (no argument) in pytorch_datasets.py:24 and :53, which re-seed from OS entropy every worker.
findings.concern: Weight init, data shuffling, dropout, and sampling are not deterministically seeded, so the single-run FID/IS values in Tables 2-3 cannot be reproduced exactly and `config.seed` is a dead knob (run-to-run FID variance is modest over 50k samples but non-zero).
findings.resolution: Apply config.seed to Python/NumPy/torch/CUDA RNGs at startup, or report FID averaged over seeds with its variance.
findings.reason: Quote matches configs/default_cifar10_configs.py:77 verbatim; a repo-wide grep for config.seed/manual_seed/set_seed found only the two seed declarations (default_cifar10_configs.py, default_lsun_configs.py) and confirmed the only consumers are argument-less np.random.seed() calls at pytorch_datasets.py:24 and :53.

findings.title: Loss target uses stop-gradient online weights, not the EMA (theta-) the equations specify
findings.quote:
model.train(train)
    model_fn = model
    
    rng_state = torch.cuda.get_rng_state()
    vt = model_fn(xt, t*999)
    
    torch.cuda.set_rng_state(rng_state) # Shared Dropout Mask
    with torch.no_grad():
      if (isinstance(hyperparameter["boundary"], int) 
          and hyperparameter["boundary"] == 0): # when hyperparameter["boundary"] == 0, vr is not needed
        vr = None
      else:
        vr = model_fn(xr, r*999)
        vr = torch.nan_to_num(vr)
findings.claim: Eq. (6)/(8)/(11) define the second (target) branch with theta- = 'the running average of past values of theta using EMA'. The code computes the target velocity vr from the current online model (`model_fn = model`) inside `torch.no_grad()` — a stop-gradient of the online weights. The maintained EMA (`state['ema']`) is applied only for sampling/eval in step_fn, never inside the loss.
findings.concern: The implemented objective uses a stop-gradient online target rather than the EMA target the paper's equations specify; this is a valid, self-consistent design (and matches Theorem 1's stated theta-=theta assumption), but it does not match the loss as written in the paper.
findings.resolution: Reconcile the paper's EMA notation with the stop-gradient online implementation, or clarify that EMA is deliberately not used in the training objective.
findings.reason: Quote matches losses.py:195-208 verbatim; model_fn=model is used for both vt and vr with no EMA substitution, while grep confirms state['ema'] appears only later (losses.py:290/293) in the sampling/step_fn path; paper_text.txt confirms the theta- / EMA wording the claim cites.
